segments: and mounted his horse, wishing (to go?) to his camp,
where his wives and his household were,
and he left the curtains and the tents pitched.
And when he had not yet gone the distance of an arrow-shot,
Brim (Burim?) struck and plundered the curtains of Gaikhatu,
and pursued after him.
And because before these things, also in calling to account the head of another myriad in the country of the Iberians,
whose name was Tukal,
Gaikhatu himself had again sent,
that one also arrived from that region near the camp of Gaikhatu.
And he found there tumults, and strifes, and divisions,
and armies pressing upon one another,
and plunderings and robberies without end.
And immediately Gaikhatu arrived with four or five souls, and Brim (Burim?) pursuing after him;
and Tukal met him in front,
and they caught him and killed him,
on the fifth day of the month of Adar of the year 1606
of the Greeks,
while Baidu was not (aware?), nor was he inclined to his destruction,
but only to seize him and imprison him in one of the fortresses.
Because when the nobles united with him and the armies submitted to him,
he sent a messenger to take Gaikhatu and bring him to him.
When the messenger arrived,
he found that he had already been put to death,
and he left and returned empty-handed.
And thus all the nobles, and sons, and daughters, and sons-in-law, and daughters-in-law,
were pressing upon one another in subjection and obedience to Baidu.
And when the majority of the nobles agreed with him,
he sent a messenger to Ghazan to come and not delay.
And because this Ghazan was situated at a distance,
and it was still the winter season,
and the roads were devoid of grass and of provisions,
Ghazan was marching with difficulty with the armies that were with him toward the region of Baidu.
Now those who were gathered with Baidu,
when they saw that Ghazan was delaying and not arriving hastily,
began to flatter Baidu, saying:
"For you indeed the kingdom is fitting;
and Ghazan is a boy young in years,
and is not sufficient to govern the kingdom of the house of Magog.
And if you turn back,
and hand over the whole administration to Ghazan,
the affair of the Mongols will end in ruin."
